images.title: Double the side, four times the area
images.purpose: Shows that stretching a 2 cm square to a 4 cm square makes 4 copies of the small square, not 2.
images.composition: One 4 by 4 square on a faint grid, with the original 2 by 2 square highlighted in its bottom left corner.
images.exact_structure: Plain white background, lots of empty space, the figure large and centred, thin dark outlines (#2B2B2B), flat fills. Only the labels listed appear; no other text, no scenery, no characters. A faint grey (#6B7280) grid of unit squares, 4 columns and 4 rows, 16 unit squares, outlined as one large square 4 units by 4 units. Thick dark lines divide it into four 2 by 2 squares. The bottom left 2 by 2 square is filled teal (#0072B2); the other three 2 by 2 squares are filled amber (#E69F00), semi light so the grid shows through. Labels: 2 cm under the bottom side of the teal square, 4 cm under the bottom side of the big square (placed below the 2 cm label), 4 cm² inside the teal square, 16 cm² beside the right side of the big square. Check: 2 × 2 = 4, 4 × 4 = 16, and 16 = 4 × 4 small squares.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
images.takeaway: When every side doubles, the area becomes 4 times as big.
images.description: Shows that stretching a 2 cm square to a 4 cm square makes 4 copies of the small square, not 2.
images.context: Practice concept with the rectangle stretcher tool; matches the square doubling exercise.
images.teaching_notes: Ask how many teal squares fit in the big square before counting.

image_decisions.why: Stretching both sides is the tool's core move; the picture shows why area grows by 4, against the doubling misconception.
